cases.option: Full native Swift/SwiftUI (AppKit where needed) rewrite of the vibemix UI
cases.strongest_case:
vibemix is not a web app that happens to be downloaded — it is an instrument that lives ON STAGE next to Rekordbox and Serato, and its entire thesis ("real DJ friend, no AI slop") is carried by surfaces the web stack is structurally worst at. The one surface everyone — including the 2026-06-05 rejection doc itself — concedes only native truly nails is the product's most public face: a non-activating, fullScreenAuxiliary NSPanel HUD floating over a fullscreen DJ app. Tauri still lacks the primitive (open issues tauri#11488/#13034); today it's bought via third-party crates working around the shell. Worse, WKWebView throttles rAF/timers for occluded and non-frontmost windows — the always-on-top pill over fullscreen Rekordbox is precisely the throttled case — while a native CADisplayLink/Metal render loop is exempt and drives 120Hz ProMotion meters. The platform winds in 2026 blow native on BOTH OSes: macOS 26's Liquid Glass makes custom-drawn web facsimiles of OS materials read more dated every release (vibemix's hand-painted "textured instrument" CSS competes against first-class glassEffect/NSVisualEffectView), and Microsoft at Build 2026 formally declared WinUI "the production platform for Windows apps" while publicly campaigning to kill "web app slop" on Windows 11. The audience — pro-audio users whose reference apps are all native C++ — can smell webview jank in a waveform.

And uniquely for THIS codebase, the rewrite is far cheaper than the scary LOC totals suggest, because the UI is already a thin client. ALL real work (audio DSP, AI brain, state) lives in the Python sidecar behind a broadcast JSON socket — `IpcRouterBus` in `src/vibemix/runtime/ws_bus.py` sends to ALL connected clients on `127.0.0.1:8765`, nothing in the protocol is Tauri-specific, and the 83-type `messages.schema.json` ports mechanically to Swift `Codable`. The engine (the actual product) reuses 100%. A native rewrite doesn't just re-skin: it DELETES whole layers — the ~9.1k-line Rust shell, the wry bridge, the ajv schema-codegen pipeline, the WKWebView-vs-WebView2 dual-engine QA matrix, and 8 separate webview surfaces (`tauri/ui/*.html`) each carrying its own JS context on a hot gig laptop already running Rekordbox + Python DSP + local Chatterbox TTS + CLAP ONNX. There's no React to unwind — the vanilla TS is already organized as windows/surfaces, which is exactly how SwiftUI scenes decompose. Bonus the rejection doc missed: `tauri.conf.json5:112` sets `macOSPrivateApi: true` (required for the transparent windows), which is a Mac App Store disqualifier — a native app needs zero private API for transparency/vibrancy, unlocking MAS distribution, IAP (a real assist on the API-key/payments problem), and the trust halo a paid desktop product wants. If vibemix intends to be "the next Serato," the end-state UI is native; the only honest argument is about WHEN.
real_wins: The pill/HUD becomes first-class: non-activating NSPanel + .fullScreenAuxiliary + tracking areas + Spaces behavior natively, instead of tauri-nspanel crates patching around missing Tauri primitives (tauri#11488/#13034 still open). This is the product's most visible surface and the one even the 2026-06-05 rejection doc admits only native truly nails.

No webview throttling on the surfaces that matter: WKWebView throttles rAF/timers for occluded/non-frontmost windows — exactly the floating pill + mascot over fullscreen Rekordbox. Native CADisplayLink/Metal render loops are exempt and drive 120Hz ProMotion waveforms/meters with lower jitter.

True OS materials that age WITH the OS: macOS 26 Liquid Glass / NSVisualEffectView first-class instead of CSS backdrop-filter facsimiles; on Windows, WinUI 3 acrylic/mica natively — and Microsoft at Build 2026 just declared WinUI THE production platform while campaigning against web-app slop (windowslatest.com 2026-06-04).

Real memory/CPU headroom on gig laptops: one native process replaces 8 webview surfaces (tauri/ui/*.html), each with its own JS heap + the three.js runtime — on a machine simultaneously running Rekordbox/Serato, the Python DSP sidecar, Chatterbox TTS, and CLAP ONNX, the UI's footprint is a genuine performance budget line, not vanity.

Mac App Store path unlocked: tauri.conf.json5:112 `macOSPrivateApi: true` (needed for transparent windows) is a MAS disqualifier today; native transparency/vibrancy uses no private API → MAS distribution, IAP, discovery, trust for a paid product.

Unusually cheap engine reuse — verified, not hoped: IpcRouterBus broadcasts JSON to all clients on 127.0.0.1:8765; a Swift app subscribes to the SAME socket the webviews use, the 83-type schema maps to Codable, and the entire Python engine (the actual product) transfers untouched. The rewrite is views-only by construction.

Deletes whole layers instead of porting them: ~9.1k lines of Rust window plumbing, the ajv codegen pipeline, and the WKWebView-vs-WebView2 cross-engine QA matrix all disappear; native a11y (VoiceOver-correct controls), real menu bar, native windowing come free instead of being maintained by hand in ARIA + custom chrome.
Brand-fit with the audience: DJs' reference software (Serato, Rekordbox, Ableton) is all native; 'instrument, not app' perceived quality compounds the anti-slop positioning.
costs: 4-7 months of focused rebuild for ~59.4k lines of non-test TS + ~12.9k CSS across 8 surfaces (measured in-repo), executed by a solo founder who doesn't write Swift, on a team whose stated priority is Bravoh — while launch is THE goal. The rewrite torches the launch window.

Discards 37.9k lines of tests / 1,577 green vitest specs — the encoded anti-slop behavioral contract (Invariant #5 idle-vs-fault guard, optimistic-repaint settings rule, citation-gated reaction UI, the pill focus dance). Each of those is a shipped bug fix that a rewrite re-discovers in production, per the classic rewrite failure mode.

The three.js GPGPU particle organism / mascot — explicitly the visual soul — has no Swift port path; Three.js→Metal/SceneKit is a research project, not a translation. It either ships degraded or blocks the rewrite's tail.

The agentic dev loop that actually builds this product (drive-vibemix skill, ws_observe MCP, vitest, Playwright screenshots) is web-tuned; Xcode-cycle agent iteration is materially slower, so the 'Claude/Codex write the Swift' mitigation is weaker than it sounds.

Migration limbo: old Tauri UI must keep shipping fixes while the native one is built (Kaan demos to Francesco/DJs continuously) — dual-maintenance is the documented stall mode (68% of strangler migrations stall <90 days per the prior decision's sources), and there is no second engineer to hold one of the two lanes.

The 'textured instrument' design contract (mocks/vibemix-bravoh-grade-pink.html, Kaan-approved 2026-06-10, 8 commits just landed) is custom-drawn, not OS chrome — so native buys the WINDOW and MATERIAL wins, but every slab, engraved label, and rose key-light still gets hand-rebuilt in SwiftUI Canvas/Metal; the 12.9k CSS doesn't translate, it re-paints.
killers: THE killer — SwiftUI/AppKit does not exist on Windows, and v1 is bindingly macOS+Windows. The researched June-2026 Swift-on-Windows reality: the TOOLCHAIN is real (officially supported since 2020; Swift.org chartered a dedicated Windows workgroup in Jan 2026), but there is no Swift UI framework for Windows — the path is writing a SECOND application against WinUI 3 through swift-winrt language projections. So 'one full native Swift rewrite' is actually TWO UI rewrites (SwiftUI on macOS + Swift/WinRT+WinUI on Windows) sharing models but zero views — on a solo team, that is roughly 1.7-2x the already-fatal cost. (Sources: swift.org/blog/whats-new-in-swift-february-2026, swift.org/install/windows, github.com/thebrowsercompany/swift-winrt, infoworld.com on Swift+WinUI.)

The Swift-on-Windows ecosystem just lost its industrial patron: The Browser Company — the entity that funded swift-winrt/swift-winui and proved the lane with Arc on Windows — was acquired by Atlassian (completed Oct 2025) to build Dia; Arc is in maintenance mode, and thebrowsercompany/swift-winui's own README now calls itself 'an outdated snapshot... provided for illustration purposes.' Betting v1 of a commercial product on that lane in 2026 is betting on an orphaned frontier toolchain. (Sources: businesswire.com Atlassian completion 2025-10-21, techcrunch.com 2025-09-04, github.com/thebrowsercompany/swift-winui.)

Constraint stack: solo engineer + Bravoh-takes-priority + tight budget + launch-is-the-goal means the four revisit-gates set in .planning/packets/2026-06-05/NATIVE-UI-DECISION.md §5 (shipped+paying users, funded native headcount, spike-proven felt delta, real Windows answer) are ALL currently unmet — the rewrite can't be funded without violating at least one binding constraint.
cases.bottom_line: The founder's instinct is RIGHT about where the web stack is weakest (the floating HUD, OS materials, webview throttling, gig-laptop footprint) and this codebase's ws-bus thin-client boundary makes a native rewrite unusually cheap for the macOS half — but 'full native Swift' under the binding macOS+Windows v1 charter is secretly TWO rewrites, because SwiftUI does not exist on Windows and the Swift/WinRT-on-WinUI lane just lost its flagship patron to the Atlassian acquisition. Verdict as advocate: native macOS is the correct END-STATE and the ws-bus boundary should be treated as the deliberate seam that keeps it cheap to do post-launch — but for v1 it is killed by the Windows constraint plus solo-engineer math; buy the genuinely-native wins surgically now (NSPanel + vibrancy on the pill) and pull the trigger on Swift only when the four §5 gates hold, starting with the pill as the one-week proof spike.

cases.option: Rewrite the vibemix UI in Flutter desktop (Dart, Impeller/Skia renderer), keeping the Python sidecar and the existing ws/JSON IPC contract untouched
cases.strongest_case:
vibemix is the rare app where Flutter's "we render every pixel ourselves" model is a pure win and the WebView's entire value proposition is dead weight. The design contract (mocks/vibemix-bravoh-grade-pink.html) uses ZERO native widgets — machined slabs, rose key-light, engraved mono labels, all custom-drawn — so Tauri buys vibemix nothing except two DIFFERENT browser engines to fight: WKWebView (Safari engine) on macOS and WebView2 (Chromium) on Windows. Every pixel of the Kaan-approved contract must be re-verified per engine; backdrop-filter, color management, WebGL throttling, and font rasterization all diverge, and the Windows half of that QA matrix is essentially unexercised today. Flutter collapses this to one GPU-accelerated renderer that is pixel-identical on both v1 platforms, and upgrades the material language itself: the rose key-light, slab speculars, and the parked GPGPU particle organism become first-class FragmentShader/CustomPainter work instead of CSS approximations and three.js-inside-WKWebView. Golden-file widget tests then turn the design contract from a vibe-checked HTML mock into a machine-enforced artifact — strictly better than today's pixelmatch arrangement.

Crucially, the rewrite scope is the UI half ONLY. The architecture already firewalls it: the Python sidecar does all real work (audio DSP, state, Sven's brain), the wire is formalized in src/ipc/messages.schema.json, and the bus is plain JSON over 127.0.0.1:8765. Regenerate Dart types from the same schema, spawn the same sidecar via Process, and Invariants 1-5 never get touched. Among the candidates only Flutter combines that with solo-dev/agent viability: Dart has by far the largest LLM training corpus of any non-web option (Claude/Codex are productive in it; Slint DSL, QML, and iced are comparative deserts), hot reload matches the agent-iterate-on-design loop, desktop is stable on Windows/macOS with Impeller landing there through 2026 (https://docs.flutter.dev/platform-integration/desktop, https://softaims.com/blog/flutter-3-impeller-wasm-features-2026), and the runtime footprint is sane — unlike Compose Multiplatform's JVM at 108-146MB for hello-world (https://github.com/JetBrains/compose-multiplatform/issues/1632). Qt/QML is the only other adult-grade option and loses on dual-language friction, LGPL/commercial licensing overhead for a signed commercial binary, and agent fit. The Rust trio self-eliminates: egui is wrong for consumer-grade typography/compositing, iced is pre-1.0 churn (https://www.boringcactus.com/2025/04/13/2025-survey-of-rust-gui-libraries.html), and gpui's Windows backend is still maturing while its API tracks Zed's internal needs (https://crates.io/crates/gpui).
real_wins: One renderer on macOS+Windows: eliminates the WKWebView-vs-WebView2 dual-engine QA matrix entirely — the approved design renders pixel-identical on both v1 platforms, and the (currently untested) Windows visual surface comes for free instead of as a second hardening pass

Design-language upgrade, not just parity: fragment shaders + CustomPainter are a strictly stronger material system than CSS for lit/textured surfaces — the rose key-light, slab speculars, and the parked curl-noise organism (rejected at 0.1/10 as a web attempt) become native GPU work at 120Hz instead of three.js fighting WKWebView throttling

The rewrite is UI-half only: the Python sidecar (all DSP/AI/state), the ws bus on 8765/8766, and messages.schema.json survive verbatim — codegen Dart instead of TS from the same schema; none of the five cardinal invariants are touched

Golden-file widget tests make the design contract machine-enforced (matchesGoldenFile per surface vs today's mock-by-eye + pixelmatch), and widget tests replace the jsdom-approximation layer with tests that exercise the real renderer

Best agent/solo-dev fit of any non-web option: huge Dart corpus in LLM training data, hot reload for design iteration, single language, first-class tooling — versus QML/Slint-DSL/iced where Claude/Codex output quality drops measurably

Sane runtime: ~30MB engine overhead, no JVM (Compose burns 108-146MB on hello-world), no Chromium; ships as a normal signable/notarizable .app + MSIX/installer, so the existing signing pipeline concept carries over
costs: Rebuild of 61,234 lines of TS + 12,952 lines of CSS across six surfaces (session deck, wizard, library/Viber, debrief, learn, settings, mascot overlay) — with agents and the sidecar untouched, realistically 2-4 months of focused solo-engineer time to true parity, not weeks

The 37,943-line test corpus (1,577 green vitest tests) is torched and must be re-expressed as widget/golden/integration_test suites; the web-tuned agent infrastructure (frontend-enforcement skill keyed to HTML mocks, vitest QA hooks, qa-blitz, Playwright e2e) all needs re-tooling

The three.js mascot/particle layer and the HTML mock workflow die: mocks/*.html stops being a 1:1 contract you can diff CSS against — the design source of truth has to migrate to golden images, a real workflow change for how Kaan approves UI

Platform-shell risk to spike FIRST: Flutter desktop multi-window (debrief is a second window on 8766) only recently matured, and the transparent always-on-top mascot overlay needs window_manager/community plugins on both OSes — feasible but the community-maintained edge of the ecosystem
Tauri/Rust shell knowledge and the shipped signed+notarized vibemix-0.0.1.dmg pipeline get partially rebuilt (sidecar bundling, provenance guard, notarization scripts re-pointed at a Flutter .app)
Opportunity cost is the real currency: every week on the rewrite is a week not spent on the actual release blocker — Sven's friend-score and the grounded-voice bar — which no renderer change improves
killers: Schedule: launch is THE goal, Kaan is a solo engineer with Bravoh taking priority, and a signed DMG already exists — a 2-4 month UI re-platform pre-launch is functionally a launch cancellation, and the 2026-06-05 evaluation already rejected a full rewrite on exactly these grounds

Wrong diagnosis: every documented UI failure (soulless shell, dark wiring, dead Viber chat, broken go-live feedback) is a design/wiring problem the teardowns trace to specific TS/Python seams — none is a WebView engine limitation; Flutter would faithfully re-implement the same problems in a new language
The dual-engine pain Flutter solves has a 10x-cheaper mitigation: a WebView2 CI lane + a constrained CSS subset costs days, not months
cases.bottom_line: Flutter desktop is the single honest winner among cross-platform candidates for vibemix — the only toolkit where a zero-native-widget, fully custom-material product gains (one pixel-identical GPU renderer on both v1 platforms, shaders as the native material primitive, golden-test-enforced design contract, sidecar untouched) while staying viable for a solo engineer driving LLM agents. But it wins the comparison, not the decision: pre-launch, the rewrite's 2-4 month bill lands entirely on the schedule of a product whose actual release blocker is voice quality, not rendering. The defensible move is Flutter as the v2 re-platform candidate — spike multi-window + transparent overlay + one shader-built deck surface in a week post-launch — and pay the WebView2 CI-lane tax now. Sources: https://docs.flutter.dev/platform-integration/desktop, https://softaims.com/blog/flutter-3-impeller-wasm-features-2026, https://github.com/JetBrains/compose-multiplatform/issues/1632, https://www.boringcactus.com/2025/04/13/2025-survey-of-rust-gui-libraries.html, https://crates.io/crates/gpui, https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-component

cases.strongest_case:

A native toolkit's one genuine gift — free system widgets — is the one thing this product deliberately doesn't use. Premium is craft, not toolkit: Raycast 2.0 migrated FROM hand-built Swift+AppKit TO React-in-a-WebView and kept its premium reputation ([Raycast deep dive](https://www.raycast.com/blog/a-technical-deep-dive-into-the-new-raycast)); Linear, VS Code, Figma, and the ChatGPT/Claude desktop apps all clear the bar on web stacks (table in .planning/packets/2026-06-05/NATIVE-UI-DECISION.md).

Meanwhile the native-feel ceiling inside Tauri is high and partially already cashed in: pill_window.rs:112-120 already applies a REAL NSVisualEffectView (window_vibrancy::apply_vibrancy, HudWindow material) — not a CSS backdrop-filter fake; mascot_window.rs, pill_window.rs, and overlay.rs already ship transparent + always-on-top + click-through floating windows; tauri.conf.json5 already runs native macOS decorations with Overlay titleBarStyle (integrated traffic lights) and macOSPrivateApi. The scoped escape valve already exists and is correctly scoped: the parked Swift Liquid-Glass pill spike talks to the same 127.0.0.1:8765 bus the webviews use (IpcRouterBus broadcasts to ALL clients; the protocol is UI-agnostic), so if one surface ever empirically proves a felt delta the crates can't reach, it can go native without touching Windows parity or the other 12 surfaces.
real_wins: Ships v1 on BOTH charter platforms (macOS + Windows) from one 61k-line codebase a solo founder already knows — no third UI, no Swift learning curve while Bravoh takes priority

Keeps the ~38k LOC / 1,500+ green-test behavioral net (the anti-slop release gate's regression armor) and the 83-type IPC codegen layer intact — these are 'collected bug fixes' a rewrite re-discovers in production

Every hour spent is product polish, not platform migration — consistent with ship-when-ready, tight budget, and Sven's voice (not the toolkit) being the actual launch-blocking quality gap

judge.rationale: Two of the three advocates convict themselves. The Swift case's own killers section concedes that under the binding macOS+Windows v1 charter, 'full native Swift' is secretly TWO rewrites (SwiftUI has no Windows existence; the Swift/WinRT+WinUI lane just lost its industrial patron to the Atlassian acquisition, with swift-winui's README self-describing as an outdated snapshot) — its bottom line is literally 'killed for v1.' Its remaining strong claims also wilt under attack: the WKWebView-throttling argument targets occluded/minimized windows, but the pill is by definition visible and always-on-top, so the genuine gap is only the non-activating panel primitive — which the repo already has a documented in-shell fix for (tauri-nspanel ~40-line recipe in NATIVE-UI-DECISION.md §4, plus a sanctioned objc2 NSPanel-subclass design already written in pill_window.rs:47-61, with vibrancy ALREADY shipped at pill_window.rs:112-117 — verified). The MAS/IAP argument is a non sequitur for v1: a signed+notarized DMG shipped 2026-06-08 and direct distribution is the plan. And 'views-only by construction' elides that the views ARE the cost — the advocate admits the 12.9k CSS textured-instrument contract doesn't translate, it re-paints. The Flutter case likewise concedes its own killers (a 2-4 month re-platform = functional launch cancellation; wrong diagnosis — every documented UI failure traces to TS/Python wiring seams, none to a WebView engine limitation; the dual-engine pain has a days-cheap WebView2 CI mitigation). Its 'golden tests strictly better' claim is wrong in practice — golden files are notoriously flaky across GPU/font rasterization, re-importing the cross-platform variance it promises to eliminate — and it torches the solo engineer's actual force multiplier: 1,577 green tests plus the entire web-tuned agent toolchain (vitest hooks, qa-blitz, Playwright, HTML-mock contract workflow). Flutter's transparent click-through overlay + multi-window needs sit on the community-plugin edge of its ecosystem — riskiest exactly at vibemix's signature surfaces. That leaves stay-Tauri, whose weaknesses are real but convert into work items rather than killers: an unexercised Windows/WebView2 visual lane, an unproven built-artifact pill over fullscreen Rekordbox, and 8 webview process trees on a gig laptop. Decisive context: the actual launch blockers are Sven's voice/perception quality (friend score, cold-start silence, empty deck) — no renderer change touches any of them, and every rewrite month is taken from the only gate that matters. I also reject hybrid-NOW: building the Swift pill today means two divergent pill implementations (Swift macOS + Tauri Windows) in a language the solo engineer doesn't write, to polish a surface no teardown lists as a blocker; hybrid is the correctly-gated escape valve, not the v1 plan. Judged fresh, the 2026-06-05 conclusion was right and its four §5 revisit gates (shipped+paying users, funded native headcount, spike-proven felt delta, real Windows answer) remain the correct trigger — all currently unmet. The ws-bus thin-client boundary is the strategic asset: it keeps a future native end-state cheap without paying for it now.
conditions: Ship the non-activating pill NOW: convert the pill window to a real NSPanel (tauri-nspanel v2.1 macro or the in-repo objc2 subclass path per pill_window.rs:47-61) with .nonactivatingPanel + .fullScreenAuxiliary + .canJoinAllSpaces, and acceptance-test it in the BUILT artifact over real fullscreen Rekordbox/Serato — zero focus-steal is the pass criterion; explicitly test the tauri-plugin-store geometry-save panic interaction (plugins-workspace #1546).

Stand up a Windows/WebView2 visual QA lane before launch (CI screenshots or a regularly-exercised Windows box): pixel-verify the pink-mock contract surfaces (backdrop-filter, fonts, canvas perf) on WebView2 — the charter says Windows is v1 and that lane is currently untested; pair with apply_acrylic/mica as the Windows vibrancy analog.

Measure and budget the 8-surface webview footprint on a gig-laptop profile (Rekordbox + Python sidecar + Chatterbox TTS + CLAP ONNX running concurrently): lazy-create secondary windows, destroy hidden surfaces, and pause/decimate the three.js render loop when occluded — make UI RAM/CPU a tracked number, not a vibe.

Keep the ws-bus/IPC seam deliberately UI-agnostic (no Tauri-specific protocol leakage into messages.schema.json or IpcRouterBus) — this is the documented exit hatch that keeps a post-launch native macOS surface cheap; treat any PR that couples the wire to the webview as a regression.

Keep the one-week Swift Liquid-Glass pill spike PARKED behind the NATIVE-UI-DECISION.md §5 gates; trigger it only post-launch, only if the nspanel pill demonstrably fails a felt-quality bar live, and judge it by A/B feel against the crate-path pill — never by vibes.

Spend every reclaimed week on the actual launch gates: Sven friend-score (bench loop), cold-start silence, fresh-user empty deck, go-live determinism — the toolkit decision is settled precisely so this work gets the time.
If Mac App Store distribution ever becomes a goal, audit the macOSPrivateApi:true usage (tauri.conf.json5:112) then — it is not a v1 item and must not be used to justify a rewrite now.
judge.strongest_counterargument: The product's single most public surface — the always-on-top pill/HUD floating over fullscreen Rekordbox, judged by pro-audio users whose reference software is uniformly native — sits exactly where the web stack is structurally weakest and where Tauri itself still lacks the primitive (tauri #11488/#13034 remain open; the fix rides third-party crates with documented panic interactions and a class-swizzle landmine the repo's own comments warn about). If the crate-path pill fails the by-feel test against fullscreen DJ software in the built artifact, 'stay' didn't avoid the native work — it deferred it to the worst possible moment: post-launch, in public, with paying DJs watching. Meanwhile the 2026 platform winds (macOS Liquid Glass, Microsoft's explicit WinUI-over-web-slop campaign) make custom-drawn web facsimiles read slightly more dated with every OS release, and the ws-bus boundary that makes staying safe is the same evidence that a native rewrite is unusually cheap HERE — engine reuse is 100%, the schema ports mechanically, and the UI is already organized as surfaces. If vibemix genuinely intends to be 'the next Serato,' native is the plausible end-state, and every additional month on Tauri adds web LOC and web-tuned tests that the eventual port must re-pay with interest — so the cheapest moment for the macOS-native pivot is always now, and it only gets more expensive.
